stem: In a cricket league in Bangladesh, every team plays every other team exactly once. If the league has \(n\) teams, the total number of matches played is \(\frac{n(n - 1)}{2}\). A season of the league had 45 matches in all. How many teams were in the league?
solution: Set the number of matches equal to 45: \(\frac{n(n - 1)}{2} = 45\), so \(n(n - 1) = 90\).
The number of teams must be positive, so \(n = 10\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(n(n - 1) = 90\) gives \(n^{2} - n - 90 = 0\), so \(n = 10\) (the other root, \(-9\), is not a number of teams).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}\) for the number of matches; with \(n\) teams each team plays \(n - 1\) others, not \(n + 1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of treating the number of matches as the number of teams instead of solving \(\frac{n(n - 1)}{2} = 45\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of doubling 45 to get \(n(n - 1) = 90\) and stopping there; 90 is \(n(n - 1)\), not \(n\).

verify:
n = symbols('n')
sols = solve(Eq(n*(n - 1)/2, 45), n)
assert sorted(sols) == [-9, 10]
assert value(choices[answer]) == 10
assert all(value(choices[k]) != 10 for k in choices if k != answer)
